behaviors.name: network
behaviors.why: Communication with external hosts or networks can expose sensitive information or provide a backdoor for attackers.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('socket.', 'requests.', 'urllib.', 'httpx.', 'aiohttp.', 'ftplib.'))

behaviors.name: network_data_reception
behaviors.why: Receiving network data can indicate data exfiltration or other malicious activity.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.endswith(('.recv', '.recvfrom', '.read'))

behaviors.name: exec_eval
behaviors.why: Executing or evaluating code can allow attackers to run arbitrary commands or scripts, potentially leading to a full system compromise.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('eval', 'exec', 'os.system', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: dns_activity
behaviors.why: DNS activity can reveal sensitive information about the target system, such as its IP address or domain name.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('socket.', 'dns.', 'resolver.'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_http
behaviors.why: Exfiltrating data over HTTP can be detected and blocked by security systems, but it can also be used to hide the exfiltration activity.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('http.', 'https.', 'aiohttp.'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_socket
behaviors.why: Exfiltrating data over sockets can be used to bypass security systems and hide the exfiltration activity.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('socket.', 'ssl.', 'tls.'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_scp
behaviors.why: Exfiltrating data over SCP can be used to transfer large amounts of data securely, but it can also be used to hide the exfiltration activity.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('scp.', 'ssh.'))

behaviors.name: data_exfil_webhook
behaviors.why: Exfiltrating data over webhooks can be used to bypass security systems and hide the exfiltration activity.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('webhook.', 'http.', 'https.'))

behaviors.name: data_collection_stdin
behaviors.why: Collecting data from stdin can be used to exfiltrate data or inject malware, potentially leading to a full system compromise.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('stdin.', 'subprocess.'))

behaviors.name: lateral_movement_ssh
behaviors.why: Using SSH for lateral movement can be used to spread malware or gain unauthorized access to other systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('ssh.', 'scp.'))

behaviors.name: self_propagation_scp
behaviors.why: Using SCP for self-propagation can be used to spread malware or gain unauthorized access to other systems.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('scp.', 'ssh.'))

behaviors.name: fs_read
behaviors.why: Reading from the file system can be used to exfiltrate data or inject malware, potentially leading to a full system compromise.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('os.', 'file.', 'open.'))

behaviors.name: fs_write
behaviors.why: Writing to the file system can be used to exfiltrate data or inject malware, potentially leading to a full system compromise.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('os.', 'file.', 'open.'))

behaviors.name: payload_dumping
behaviors.why: Dumping payloads can be used to exfiltrate data or inject malware, potentially leading to a full system compromise.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: n.startswith(('json.', 'yaml.', 'pickle.'))

behaviors.name: credential_access
behaviors.why: Functions that access or manipulate credentials can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as credential stuffing or password cracking.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('os.getenv', 'os.getpass', 'getpass.getuser', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: command_execution
behaviors.why: Functions that execute commands can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as command injection or privilege escalation.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('subprocess.run', 'os.system', 'exec'))

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_exec
behaviors.why: Functions that execute dynamic code can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as code injection or command injection.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('exec', 'os.system', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: dynamic_code_load
behaviors.why: Functions that load dynamic code can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as code injection or command injection.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('import', 'exec', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: reflection_abuse
behaviors.why: Functions that use reflection can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as code injection or command injection.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('reflect', 'inspect'))

behaviors.name: crypto_activity
behaviors.why: Functions that perform cryptographic operations can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as encryption or decryption of sensitive data.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('hashlib', 'cryptography', 'ssl', 'aes', 'des'))

behaviors.name: deobfuscation
behaviors.why: Functions that deobfuscate code or data can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as code injection or data exfiltration.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('base64', 'json', 'yaml', 'zlib'))

behaviors.name: obfuscation_dynamic_config
behaviors.why: Functions that dynamically configure obfuscation can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as code injection or data exfiltration.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('obfuscation', 'dynamic_config'))

behaviors.name: system_recon
behaviors.why: Functions that perform system reconnaissance can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as gathering information about the system or network.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('os.getenv', 'os.getpass', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: process_recon
behaviors.why: Functions that perform process reconnaissance can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as gathering information about running processes or injecting malicious code.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('psutil', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: permission_manipulation
behaviors.why: Functions that manipulate permissions can potentially be exploited for attacks, such as escalating privileges or gaining unauthorized access.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('os.setuid', 'os.setgid', 'subprocess.run'))

behaviors.name: persistence
behaviors.why: Actions that attempt to persist data or code, potentially allowing attacks or introducing security vulnerabilities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('persistence_registry', 'persistence_cron', 'keylogging'))

behaviors.name: user_input_prompt
behaviors.why: Actions that prompt user input, potentially allowing attacks or introducing security vulnerabilities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('user_input_prompt', 'clipboard_abuse'))

behaviors.name: gui_abuse
behaviors.why: Actions that abuse GUI functionality, potentially allowing attacks or introducing security vulnerabilities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('gui_abuse', 'screenshot'))

behaviors.name: install_hook
behaviors.why: Actions that install hooks, potentially allowing attacks or introducing security vulnerabilities.
behaviors.rule: lambda n: any(x in n for x in ('install_hook',))
